text: The lessons began at once, starting with Bernices appearance, since Marjorie insisted that her cousins eyebrows needed shaping and her hair needed better care. <break time="0.8s" /> She also told Bernice to be especially kind to the clumsy, unpopular boys whom the other girls tried hard to avoid on the dance floor. <break time="0.8s" /> Most important of all was a bold question that Marjorie taught her to ask at dinner, Do you think I ought to bob my hair. <break time="0.8s" /> In those days, bobbed hair was considered daring, even shocking, so a girl who merely talked about cutting hers was certain to attract attention. <break time="0.8s" /> At the next dinner dance, Bernice tried the question on the young man beside her, and to her delight, he responded with eager, excited interest. <break time="0.8s" /> She promised that she would announce the date of the haircut, and she invited all the boys at the table to come and watch it happen. <break time="0.8s" /> Word of the daring girl from Eau Claire spread quickly, and before the evening ended, several boys had cut in on her for the very first time. <break time="0.8s" /> Dancing in the arms of yet another partner, Bernice felt a thrill she had never known, the dizzy pleasure of being wanted by the crowd.
